title: Witr in many ways
hookLine: one, three, or more units, prayed in different ways

lines: THREE, OR ONE, OR TWO THEN ONE.
cards: It's late. The house is dark except for one lamp. Someone who has already prayed the night prayer stands up once more before bed, for one last short prayer.

In one home it's three units, with a quiet supplication tucked inside the third. In another it's a single unit, standing alone. In a third, two units, a pause and a greeting of peace, and then one more.
All three would tell you the same thing: they're closing the night with an odd number. Today, witr, the odd prayer, and the many ways to pray it.

teach.b: Witr means odd, the opposite of even. In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ says that Allah is witr, one, and loves what is odd. The prayer carries the same word.
In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ibn Umar reports the Prophet's answer: the night prayer is prayed two units by two, and when someone fears the dawn is near, they pray one unit to make the whole odd.
And in Sunan Abi Dawud, a report gives the choice outright: whoever wishes may pray witr with five, or with three, or with one. The odd number is fixed. The shape is open.
Hanafi scholars teach that witr is wajib, a duty just below the obligatory prayers, prayed as three units joined with one closing greeting, and a supplication, the qunut, before bowing in the third.
Shafi'i and Hanbali scholars count it as a strongly encouraged sunna; its smallest form is a single unit, and three may be prayed as two, a greeting, then one.
Maliki teaching has a single unit of witr, following a pair of units prayed first. In the Ja'fari school, witr is a single unit that closes the night prayer, with a qunut of its own.
Each of these is odd, and each closes the night. The people in those three homes stand at different angles to the same instruction, and each can show you the report they're standing on.

how: Witr is prayed after the night prayer and before dawn: Hanafis as three joined units with qunut, treating it as wajib; Shafi'is and Hanbalis as one or more odd units, often two and then one; Malikis as one unit after a pair; Ja'fari Shia as a single unit with qunut closing the night prayer.

games.q: what does “witr in many ways” mean?
o: the odd-numbered prayer that closes the night, in each school's shape
a short supplication said while standing in the dawn prayer
the long extra prayers said each night of Ramadan, two by two

games.q: witr in many ways — tap the pairs.
p: two by two, then one before dawn
three units joined, qunut in the third

s: witr must always be exactly three units
a report in Sunan Abi Dawud allows five, three or one; the schools pray it in different shapes.
a report in Sahih Muslim says Allah is witr and loves what is odd
the prayer's name comes from that word: odd.
Hanafi scholars treat witr as an optional extra like any other
they call it wajib, a duty just below the obligatory prayers.

games.q: you're praying the night prayer two units at a time, and you sense the dawn is close. what does Ibn Umar's report say to do?
o: pray one unit to make the whole odd.
pray two more to keep it even.
games.why: pray one unit to make the whole odd, Ibn Umar reports. that single unit is witr, closing the night.

practice: If you pray, bring tonight's witr to mind in your school's shape, and how it closes the night. If you don't, count three slow breaths now, and let the third be the longest, the one that closes the set. Then rest.

wordCard.voice: Witr in many ways. The odd prayer that closes the night: one, three or more units, prayed in each school's own shape. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: odd, single; the name of the odd-numbered prayer that closes the night.

carryVoice: Your line: odd, in any way. A week of the plain sense, the Amman Message, hands, amin, touch, the moon and witr. Rest well.
